quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
questions.explanation: You must stop for any person using a white cane or guide dog who is crossing the street. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Look behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and make other vehicles move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, always check that no vehicles are in your way. Look behind and to the side of your vehicle before you move into a new lane.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road gets narrower ahead.
There are many curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are many curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to what is coming. This sign warns you about a winding road with curves.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is turning right and you also need to turn right, you should:

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus moves.
Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning first.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning first.
questions.explanation: Never try to squeeze your vehicle between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus has finished its turn before you turn.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Turn up your radio louder.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of tiredness while driving. If you are struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting from your lane, or using the radio to stay awake, you are too tired to drive safely. Find a safe parking spot and rest with a short nap.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brake pedal quickly several times.
Slow down gradually without braking hard.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking hard.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep your vehicle straight. Take your foot off the gas and do not brake hard. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: When you are following a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Keep at least three to four seconds of distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. If a motorcyclist falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting them. This is especially important on wet, icy, gravel, or slippery roads.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to any car already in the roundabout.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by their:

options.text: Reckless and unsafe lane changes.
Number of passengers in the car.
Tendency to drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reckless and unsafe lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers on the road. If you notice a driver making reckless or unsafe lane changes, do not challenge them. The safest thing to do is get out of their way.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks traffic flow?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash scene.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash scene.
questions.explanation: Looking at crashes while driving slows down traffic and causes congestion. Do not slow down to look at accidents or unusual things on the road.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A downward-facing triangle is always a yield sign. You must be ready to slow down or stop when you see a yield sign.

questions.question: What should you do when you reach a traffic light that is not working?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and yield before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, get it off the road and away from traffic if possible. Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.question: When should you yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave at you first.
Only if the pedestrians are not using a phone.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Always come to a complete stop at a crosswalk to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection. You may proceed carefully only when your path is completely clear.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Follow other cars too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, focus on your driving and do not take other drivers' actions personally. Be realistic about travel time, drive at the speed limit, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
Drink something with caffeine.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, take a break every hour on long trips. If possible, share driving with another person so you can rest while they drive.

questions.question: If you have had several beers, the only way to reduce the effects of alcohol is to:

options.text: Take a cold shower.
Wait several hours.
Drink several cups of coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait several hours.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to remove the effects of one drink.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your lane.
Look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check behind you. Look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Also check that no other drivers are trying to move into that same spot from another lane.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is always safe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
How fast you drive does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because it frustrates drivers behind you, who may make unsafe moves to pass you. Drive with the flow of traffic and stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: Which statement is true about changing lanes?

options.text: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check all mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is in the next lane.

questions.question: If you drive slower than other traffic, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and get a ticket.
Help traffic flow better.
Show defensive driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Slow down in heavy traffic or bad weather, but do not block traffic by driving too slowly. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, unless traffic is speeding above the legal limit.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and pass many cars, you will:

options.text: Reach your destination faster and more safely.
Increase your chance of a crash.
Reduce traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Each time you pass, your risk of a crash goes up.

questions.question: Before returning to your original lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, look for both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. Only then is it safe to return to your original lane.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. Buckle your lap belt even if you have an automatic shoulder belt.

questions.question: Reaction time is slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. Alcohol makes your judgment worse and decreases your driving skills. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and the movement of other vehicles.

questions.question: In a vehicle with airbags, the safest place for children age 12 and under is:

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pickup truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Airbags help protect adults but can seriously injure children. Children age 12 and under should always sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: If you see animals near the roadway while driving, you should:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down if you see animals near the roadway. They may suddenly run or change direction. Some animals travel in groups, so more may be out of sight near the road.

questions.question: Changing lanes is best done:

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Gradually and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes gradually and carefully. Only change lanes when you must. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: Drivers are required to obey instructions from:

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Other drivers with broken-down vehicles.
Flaggers at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers at construction sites.
questions.explanation: Drivers must obey flaggers and their instructions. Flaggers are there to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: What could happen if you take a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unfit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unfit to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair your driving ability. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, you should look:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look both left and right for vehicles and pedestrians. Look left again because vehicles from your left will be closer. Check across the entire intersection to make sure it is clear.

questions.question: Traffic control devices in construction and maintenance areas are the color:

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. Use extra caution when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers on a roadway.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic must stay in the right lane.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes left or right. Stay in the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic. Never back up or make a U-turn on interstate highways. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: The driver ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Cautiously pass at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk. Pedestrians you cannot see may be crossing. Stop and only proceed after all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get in the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust mirrors, your seat, and fasten your belt before driving. Do not adjust mirrors while your vehicle is moving.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians. You must stop for them even if they are crossing illegally or in the wrong place.

questions.question: What does a red octagon-shaped sign say?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means "Stop." You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Passing cars.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. You may only turn left when it is safe and you do not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A triangular yellow sign means no passing zone. It appears on the left side of two-lane roads where you cannot pass other vehicles.
